A RodConstraint constrains two Attachments to remain separated by the value specified by Length. While the attachments remain at a set distance from one another they can both rotate freely.

A SpringConstraint applies a force to its Attachment based on spring and damper behavior. Assuming the SpringConstraint has non-zero stiffness, it will apply forces based on how far apart the Attachments are. If the Attachments are further apart than the FreeLength then the Attachments will be forced together. If they are closer than the FreeLength then the Attachments will be forced apart. In addition, if Damping is set then there will be a component to the applied force that's proportional and opposite to the velocity of the attachments.
A TorsionSpringConstraint applies a torque to its Attachment based on spring and damper behavior. Assuming the TorsionSpringConstraint has non-zero stiffness, it will apply forces based on the angle between the secondary axes of Attachments. In addition, if Damping is set then there will be a component to the applied force that's proportional and opposite to the relative angular velocity of the attachments.

Decl
DeclProtoP
Declaration
DeclareField
Declares the interval in ms between two backup polls on client channels. These polls are run in the timer thread so that gRPC can process connection failures while there is no active polling thread. They help reconnect disconnected client channels (mostly due to idleness), so that the next RPC on this channel won't fail. Set to 0 to turn off the backup polls.
Declares which DNS resolver to use. The default is ares if gRPC is built with c-ares support. Otherwise, the value of this environment variable is ignored.
Declares which polling engines to try when starting gRPC. This is a comma-separated list of engines, which are tried in priority order first -> last.

EXPERIMENTAL.  A counter of resources received that were considered invalid.
EXPERIMENTAL.  A counter of resources received that were considered valid.  The counter will be incremented even for resources that have not changed.
EXPERIMENTAL.  A counter of xDS servers going from healthy to unhealthy.  A server goes unhealthy when we have a connectivity failure or when the ADS stream fails without seeing a response message, as per gRFC A57.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of LB picks failed due to either a failed RLS request or the RLS channel being throttled.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of LB picks sent to each RLS target.  Note that if the default target is also returned by the RLS server, RPCs sent to that target from the cache will be counted in this metric, not in grpc.rls.default_target_picks.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of LB picks sent to the default target.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of endpoints from each scheduler update that don't yet have usable weight information (i.e., either the load report has not yet been received, or it is within the blackout period).

EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of failed connection attempts.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of scheduler updates in which there were not enough endpoints with valid weight, which caused the WRR policy to fall back to RR behavior.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of successful connection attempts.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of times the selected subchannel becomes disconnected.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Number of xDS resources.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Size of the RLS cache.
EXPERIMENTAL.  The histogram buckets will be endpoint weight ranges.  Each bucket will be a counter that is incremented once for every endpoint whose weight is within that range. Note that endpoints without usable weights will have weight 0.
EXPERIMENTAL.  Whether or not the xDS client currently has a working ADS stream to the xDS server.  For a given server, this will be set to 0 when we have a connectivity failure or when the ADS stream fails without seeing a response message, as per gRFC A57.  It will be set to 1 when we receive the first response on an ADS stream.
